[tool_result] # Pit-Lane Loss Model ## Formula The pit-lane loss model decomposes into three components: **L_pit = (t_entry + t_exit - t_bypass) + t_stop** Where the total loss combines entry/exit overhead (minus the time saved by bypassing the track) plus the stationary service time. ## Flag Discount Factor Under safety conditions, an effective multiplier applies: - **Green flag**: φ = 1.00 (full loss) - **Virtual Safety Car**: φ ≈ 0.60–0.70 (40–30% reduction) - **Safety Car**: φ ≈ 0.30–0.45 (70–55% reduction) Expected pit loss becomes: **L_pit^flag = φ × L_pit** ## Typical Pit Delta Values The document provides circuit-specific examples: | Circuit | Green Loss (s) | VSC Multiplier | SC Multiplier | |---------|----------------|----------------|---------------| | Monza | 18–20 | 0.65 | 0.40 | | Silverstone | 23–25 | 0.65 | 0.40 | | Monaco | 18–20 | 0.70 | 0.45 | | Spa-Francorchamps | 21–23 | 0.60 | 0.35 | | Suzuka | 22–24 | 0.65 | 0.40 | **Key note**: The document advises replacing these "illustrative priors" with actual telemetry data. The core loop calls `runStint()` per stint, applies pit-event state mutations to `finalState` between stints, and accumulates a typed timeline. No new simulation physics are needed -- only sequencing and bookkeeping. - **Pit-lane loss follows the standard formula** `L_pit = (t_entry + t_exit - t_bypass) + t_stop` with circuit-specific parameters. Typical green-flag pit deltas: 18-25 seconds. Under VSC multiply by ~0.65, under SC by ~0.40, red flag = free tire change.
